Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaCorp Global Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star one to ask a question, and you will be prompted to provide your name and company. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaCorp Global's Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. NovaCorp Global delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, which highlights robust top-line growth and margin expansion; brand performance and innovation driving market share gains; supply chain and operational efficiency yielding significant savings; marketing and promotional activities with strong returns; sustainability initiatives advancing our ESG goals; digital transformation accelerating e-commerce; sales performance and channel strategy expanding distribution; and our outlook for the remainder of the year with raised guidance.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide more detail on our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $18.2 billion, representing a 6% increase on a reported basis and 8% organically compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, up 170 basis points year-over-year, driven by pricing discipline, favorable product mix, and productivity gains. Operating income was $850 million, up 12%, and diluted earnings per share were $1.42, reflecting 11% adjusted growth. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me unpack our overall company performance highlights for Q3 FY2024, which really underscore NovaCorp Global's continued resilience and execution in this dynamic CPG landscape. We've navigated persistent inflation, supply chain headwinds, and shifting consumer behaviors toward premiumization, innovation, and operational agility. Starting with the top line, Q3 net sales reached $18.2 billion, up 6% reported and 8% organic, excluding a 2% foreign exchange headwind. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth, outpacing the global CPG industry average of 4% according to NielsenIQ data. Volume grew 2%, driven by high-margin categories, while price/mix added a robust 6%, reflecting disciplined pricing amid 5-7% input cost inflation in areas like palm oil and PET resin. This stacks up well against peers like Procter & Gamble at 4% organic and Unilever at 5%.

By segment, our Beauty & Personal Care division led with $6.8 billion in sales, up 10% organically, thanks to 120 basis points of market share gains in North American hair care per IRI scans from our relaunched PureGlow shampoo line with 95% naturally derived ingredients capturing 15% category share. Home Care followed at $5.1 billion, plus 7% organic, boosted by productivity savings offsetting 8% logistics increases, with EcoShield laundry pods in recyclable packaging seeing 25% volume uplift as consumers traded up to sustainable options. Food & Beverages rounded out at $6.3 billion, up 6% organic, with snacks and plant-based proteins shining—VitaFuel bars grew 18%, gaining 80 basis points share against Kellogg and Mondelez per Circana.

Gross margins expanded 210 basis points to 53.2% blended, our highest in five years, powered by $450 million in supply chain savings from Operation Zero Waste, including AI-optimized procurement via SAP Ariba partnership reducing raw material waste by 12%, and $200 million from manufacturing footprint rationalization like idling two legacy European plants and shifting to lower-cost sites in Mexico and Vietnam. Adjusted operating margins hit 22.1%, up 140 basis points, despite $150 million in transitory inflation and FX impacts. Diluted EPS was $1.42, up 12% adjusted, beating guidance, with free cash flow at $2.1 billion or 115% of adjusted net earnings, funding $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a 5% dividend increase to $0.85 per share—our 28th consecutive hike.

Regionally, North America at $9.5 billion grew 7% organically, with e-commerce now 28% of sales up from 22%, driven by Amazon and Walmart+ same-day delivery for essentials like FreshStart wipes. Europe was flat at $4.2 billion due to 3% FX from a softening euro, but we gained 90 basis points share in UK household care per Kantar despite phosphate regulations. Emerging markets contributed $4.5 billion, up 14% organic: Latin America surged 18% on Brazil personal care volumes, Asia-Pacific 12% led by India where SunnySmile toothpaste doubled distribution to 1.2 million outlets via Blinkit quick-commerce.

Strategically, these results reflect our CPG 2.0 playbook: premiumization now 45% of portfolio versus 35% in 2022 with 20% ROI on innovation; digital transformation via Consumer360 platform using machine learning for personalized marketing boosting repeat rates 15%; and sustainability leadership with 65% recyclable packaging ahead of 2030 net-zero, aligning with EU directives. Looking ahead, we're raising FY24 organic sales guidance to 7-8% and adjusted EPS to $5.65-$5.75, implying 10% growth, mindful of Middle East cocoa disruptions and potential U.S. tariffs, but diversified with a $3 billion hedging book as IRI projects flat U.S. CPG volumes.

Diving deeper into Q3 organic sales growth decomposition—volume, price, and mix—which totaled a robust 5.2%, our sixth straight quarter of positive growth accelerating 110 basis points from Q2's 4.1%. This highlights resilience of billion-dollar brands like NovaCrunch snacks, PureFlow beverages, and SparkleClean cleaners amid choppy macro with inflation and softening sentiment.

Volume growth was +2.1%, up 80 basis points, from innovation in health-and-wellness like high-protein NovaCrunch bars and zero-sugar PureFlow, gaining 1.2 points North American salty snack share per Nielsen via Protein Punch relaunch with 12% distribution uplift at Walmart and Kroger. Emerging markets starred at +5.4% volume in Latin America and Asia-Pacific, Brazil SparkleClean sachets up 15% penetration, India PureFlow tetra packs via micro-entrepreneur networks. North America flat +0.8% after pruning 3% low-velocity SKUs, Europe +1.2% pressured by energy costs but countered by UEFA Euro promotions. AI-powered RGM platform boosted shelf velocity 7%, e-commerce volume +22% now 18% of sales from Prime Day and DTC.

Price realization +2.5% recovered 85% of COGS inflation from 11% YoY ag inputs like cocoa and palm oil via El Niño, with forward contracts hedging 70% FY24 needs through ADM and Cargill. Modest 3-5% increases on 60% portfolio, elasticity at -0.7 better than peers. Emerging +4.2% on trade-up, North America +1.8% with NovaRewards, Europe +3.1% eco-surcharges. Shifting to value-based pricing using NPS for sustainable premiums like Unilever's.

Mix +0.6%, highest in two years, from 2.5 points uplift to power brands now 72% sales, NovaCrunch clusters +28% ASP up 4%, phasing commoditized soaps. APAC +1.2% collagen PureFlow, North America +0.8% away-from-home rebound. Mix Mastery with IRI data secured 4,200 Costco facings, 40% recyclable packaging.

This positions for 4-6% full-year, Q4 volume from holiday launches, margins +120 bps to 22.4%, core EPS +8.2%, with GenAI promotions and fermentation partnerships.

On organic sales growth rate, it was 4.2% for the quarter ahead of 3-4% guide, fifth consecutive acceleration, raising full-year to 4-5% from 3.5-4.5% on pricing, volume, innovation. Strips FX -150 bps, acquisitions like organic snacks, divestitures. Outpaced CPG 1.8%. 2.1% volume strongest in years, 2.1% price/mix, premium Elevate line +15% penetration.

Segments: Snacks 45% sales +5.8% led by salty +110 bps share, Chewy Bites 12% distribution; Beverages 30% +3.9%, Quench+ +22%; Household 25% +2.1% refill pods +4%. North America 60% +5.5%, e-comm 18%; EMEA 20% +2.8%; APAC 12% +4.1% India +11%; LATAM 8% flat.

Core+Growth: innovation 25% sales last three years AI formulations waste -15%; route-to-market 92% ACV geospatial; premiumization NPS +8 ESG 50% recycled.

Q3 organic 4-4.5%, H2 acceleration.

Gross margin at 48.2%, up 170 bps YoY from 46.5%, 80 bps sequential, strongest expansion in three years via Margin Momentum 2025, ahead of peers 45-47%.

Tailwinds: pricing +220 bps 4-6% on ZestCrunch PureFlow, trade optimization AI -150 bps promo; mix +110 bps premium VitaGlow 15% beverages, EcoShield; productivity +90 bps RPA 12 plants 8% savings, Farm-to-Factory hedges 10% below spot cocoa palm, Maersk freight -12%.

Headwinds: input inflation -140 bps dairy +18% oils +22% PET +15% El Niño; FX -30 bps LATAM APAC.

Regions: NA 55% +240 bps 51.3%; EMEA 22% +120 bps 45.8% local sunflower; APAC -50 bps 44.2% countered JVs; LATAM 46.5%.

Toward FY24 47.5-48.5%, FY25 +100-150 bps AI pricing RevPro 70% SKUs, zero-based chain $250M consolidate 15% suppliers, R&D high-margin wellness.

Q4 48.5-49.0% commodities moderate.

For organic sales growth guidance, full year 4-5% tightening from 3-6%, on Q3 4.2% with 2.8 pts pricing 1.4 volume/mix, YTD 4.3%. Net pricing 2.5-3 pts lapping hikes offset 12-15% cocoa palm PET; volume/mix 1.5-2 pts innovation distribution. Conservatism on categories downtrading.

Price elasticity averaged -0.75 improved from -0.92 YoY -0.85 Q2, enabling 5.2% net price vs category 3.8% NielsenIQ. From brand investments, trade optimization, premium mix.

Beverages 35% -1.15 better -1.28, Zest Cola -1.05 +2.3 share low-sugar, hydration -0.65; AI engine IRI UPC -12% promo waste.

Snacks 28% -0.82 from -0.95, CrunchBar -0.72 private label Aldi, chocolate -0.55 sustainability; NA -0.78 Europe -0.95 countered loyalty.

Household 37% -0.48 inelastic, UltraClean -0.42 vs category -3.4%, shampoos -0.65 e-comm +4x.

Regions: NA 55% -0.82 private label Walmart volumes -2.1% +420 bps margin; Europe 25% -0.68 EDLP -0.45; EM 20% LATAM -0.95 sachets +8%, APAC -0.72 India -0.40.

Secular less elastic from -1.05, media +10% YoY repeats +3 to 68%, premium 42% vs 35%. Value with Virtue, Elasticity Model ML Nielsen Circana 5% accuracy, blockchain Europe. FY24 -0.70--0.80 +200 bps margin 4-6% growth 15% ROIC.

A&P spend $1.28B up 4% constant currency 13.2% sales delever from 13.8% efficiency inflation 6-8% commodities. Trade 55% $704M flat Walmart Kroger; consumer promo 20% $256M +12% Ibotta value Core Snacks +10 bps LFL.

Media 25% $320M TV OOH -8% $112M digital +25% $208M CTV $85M Roku Zest relaunch, social $60M Meta TikTok Google CPM $12.50 -15% DSP Trade Desk.

ROI ROMI 2.7x up 2.4x MMM Kantar zero-party 15M users $2.70 NMV +140 bps 3.2% growth. Beverages Zest 3.8x TikTok UGC 2.5B impressions +18% conv +50 bps Pepsi; personal 2.1x influencers.

NA $680M 3.1x omnichannel Amazon Instacart +22% basket; EMEA $320M 2.3x GDPR UK wars hyper-local +1% volume; APAC LATAM $280M 2.5x India Diwali 4.2x Brazil CTV.

Precision A&P Salesforce Einstein Snowflake 1.5PB data 30% faster testing +15-20% ROMI; retail media $150M Walmart Amazon $100B opp; sustainability 40% creative net-zero millennials 65% IRI 1.8x premium.

Summary financials: Q3 $4.8B net rev +8% reported +6% organic 3% volume 3% pricing, acq +2% EcoFresh. Beverages +9% 5% vol +1.2 share energy nootropics; Personal flat 4% price -4% vol private label; Household +7% premium pods +2.5 share EPA.

Gross +210 bps 48.2% $180M productivity Supply Chain 2.0 AI Blue Yonder 8.2x turns $50M network, pricing >2% input LATAM. Op income +12% $850M margin +110 bps 17.7% SG&A -80 bps 20.5% zero-based -15% agency GCB Media Lab $120M A&P recyclable 68% Gen Z.

EPS $1.42 +14% reported +11% adj -$0.08 restr; FCF $650M 130% adj NI $400M buybacks 2% div $0.65 47th hike.

Regions: NA 62% +7% share +0.8 IRI e-comm DTC 18% +25%; EMEA flat 2% price -2% vol +12% France; APAC +10% India Indonesia Shakti +15%; LATAM +5% Brazil Natura.

Outlook FY23 organic 5-6% prev 4-5%, op margin +140-160 bps prev 100-120, EPS $5.65-5.75 prev 5.50-5.60, FCF $2.3-2.4B 105-110%. Q4 organic 4-5% vol inflect CPI 3%, margins mid-48s $70M Zero Waste Scope 3 -20% Unilever Regen.

Pillars 2024: premium health 65% pipeline FreshStart Collagen $200M A&P IRI 2x; digital OmniChannel Salesforce Google 20% e-comm +15% AUR; sustainability 100% recyclable 2028 rPET ROI 25% YouGov.

Q3 precision execution outperform CPG index flat YTD S&P.

Next, Lisa will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, John. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our new Zest Your Day campaign for beverages, which leveraged connected TV and social media to drive 3.8x ROMI and reclaim share in zero-sugar segments. Our sustainability messaging around recyclable packaging has resonated, boosting NPS by 8 points among millennials, and we've optimized trade promotions with AI to protect margins while growing household penetration.

Following Lisa, Mike will discuss supply chain performance.

Mike Patel:
Thank you. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. Highlights include RPA in 12 plants for 8% conversion savings, Farm-to-Factory hedging below spot for cocoa and palm, and Maersk freight cuts of 12% despite Red Sea issues. We're also focused on reducing our carbon footprint through Operation Zero Waste and Scope 3 reductions via Regen Ag-like supplier programs, targeting 20% emissions cut by 2025.

After Mike, Dr. Elena will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent product launch, VitaGlow protein shakes and PureGlow clean beauty shampoos, has been well-received by consumers, capturing 15% beverage revenue share and 120 bps in hair care, with 25% of sales now from launches in the last three years using AI formulations for taste and shelf life.

Finally, Tom will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 28% of North America sales with 20% comps via Amazon and Walmart+, and total store coverage at 92% ACV using geospatial analytics. We're also investing in retail partnerships, securing 4,200 incremental facings in club channels and quick-commerce in India for 15% rural penetration growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Emily. Sustainability is core to our innovation pipeline, with 65% recyclable packaging already, ahead of 2030 net-zero, and products like EcoShield pods and rPET beverages verified under EPA Safer Choice. We've seen 25% volume uplift in these, 2.5 share points vs. Tide and Method, resonating with 68% Gen Z per NielsenIQ. Our circular pilots in APAC yield 25% ROI, enhancing brand equity while tying into A&P for 1.8x ROMI premium.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Hargrove:
Thanks, David. International is a growth engine, with emerging markets up 14% organic, APAC +12% via India quick-commerce doubling SunnySmile outlets, LATAM +18% Brazil premium skincare Natura-style, and Shakti networks +15% sachets. We're targeting $5-10 unit tiers with 20% higher velocity, joint ventures in India like Hindustan Unilever, and nearshoring Mexico for 6% volumes, aiming for EM to drive H2 acceleration.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Morgan Stanley.

Rachel Kim:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

John Ramirez:
Absolutely, Rachel. Inflation remains a focus, but our elasticity at -0.75 shows resilience, better than peers, supporting 5.2% net pricing recovering 85% COGS via 3-5% hikes with -0.7 coefficient. Volumes held with innovation shielding, like hydration -0.65, UltraClean -0.42 despite dairy +18% oils +22%. Value-based pricing on sustainable premiums 8-10%, and AI RevPro for dynamic adjustments, positioning for 2.5-3 pts FY pricing as CPI moderates.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Brian Patel with Barclays.

Brian Patel:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

Mike Patel:
Good one, Brian. AI is transformative: RGM platform +7% shelf velocity, Blue Yonder demand sensing 8.2x turns, SAP Ariba procurement -12% waste, Einstein Snowflake for A&P testing +15-20% ROMI. Elasticity Model ML on Nielsen Circana predicts within 5%, and IRI Symphony for UPC pricing cuts promo waste 12%. These drove $450M savings, $180M productivity, runway for Q4 margins mid-48s.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaCorp Global Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Decomposition of organic sales growth: v: Q3 organic sales growth decomposed as volume +2.1% (driven by innovation and emerging markets), price +2.5% (recovering 85% of COGS inflation), mix +0.6% (favoring power brands and premiums), totaling 5.2%. Earlier overview cited 2% volume and 6% price/mix for 8% organic.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth rate: Q3 organic sales growth of 8% (6% reported), marking ninth consecutive quarter, outpacing industry average of 4%; specific mentions of 4.2-5.2% with details.
aspect_summary.Gross margin percentage: Q3 gross margin of 48.2%, up 170 basis points YoY (also cited as +210 bps to 53.2% blended in parts), driven by pricing, mix, and productivity gains; highest in five years.
aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for next q: Raised FY24 full-year organic sales guidance to 7-8% (from prior 4-5% or 3-6%); Q4 guidance 4-5%; positioned for H2 acceleration.
aspect_summary.Price elasticity observations: Average price elasticity of -0.75 (improved from -0.92 YoY and -0.85 Q2), better than peers at -0.7 to -1.0; varies by segment (e.g., household -0.48 inelastic, beverages -1.15) and region; supports pricing amid inflation.
aspect_summary.A&P (advertising & promotion) spend and: A&P spend $1.28B, up 4% to 13.2% of sales; ROMI 2.7x (up from 2.4x); trade 55%, media 25% (digital +25%), consumer promo 20%; strong ROI in beverages (3.8x), precision targeting boosts efficiency.
